question: What best describes raw, unorganized facts collected from clinical observations?
explanation: Data consists of unorganized facts and figures before they are processed and given context. [learn more](GST319_U1_T1#GST319_U1_T1_h1)

question: Why is relying on data important for nursing quality improvement?

options.A: It replaces guesswork with verifiable facts
options.B: It eliminates the need for clinical judgment
options.C: It speeds up medication administration times
options.D: It reduces the total number of hospital staff

explanation: Data provides concrete evidence to guide changes rather than relying on assumptions. [learn more](GST319_U1_T1#GST319_U1_T1_h1)

question: Which of the following is an example of quantitative clinical data?
explanation: Quantitative data involves measurable numerical values like temperature and blood pressure. [learn more](GST319_U1_T1#GST319_U1_T1_h2)

question: Descriptive feedback gathered from patient interviews represents what type of data?
explanation: Qualitative data captures descriptive, non-numerical insights about experiences and perceptions. [learn more](GST319_U1_T1#GST319_U1_T1_h2)

question: What is the primary risk of inconsistent data recording practices in a ward?
explanation: Inconsistent recording introduces bias and errors, leading to false conclusions during quality analysis. [learn more](GST319_U1_T1#GST319_U1_T1_h3)

question: Which method is commonly used by nurses to gather reliable clinical data?
explanation: Clinical audits systematically review care practices against established standards to gather reliable data. [learn more](GST319_U1_T1#GST319_U1_T1_h3)

question: What tool is best used to track clinical performance trends over time?
explanation: Run charts display data points sequentially over time to help teams spot trends and patterns. [learn more](GST319_U1_T1#GST319_U1_T1_h4)

question: Why do quality improvement teams visualize data using charts and graphs?

options.A: To easily spot performance gaps and trends
options.B: To hide negative clinical outcomes from management
options.C: To increase the workload of staff nurses
options.D: To replace the need for formal nursing reports

explanation: Visual displays allow teams to quickly interpret data and evaluate whether interventions are effective. [learn more](GST319_U1_T1#GST319_U1_T1_h4)

question: A major barrier to effective data collection in many local health facilities is...
explanation: Many facilities still depend on paper-based systems which are prone to damage, loss, and difficult retrieval. [learn more](GST319_U1_T1#GST319_U1_T1_h5)

question: How can bedside nurses actively improve local health data quality?

options.A: By prioritizing accurate shift handovers and records
options.B: By relying solely on patient memory
options.C: By refusing to document routine patient vitals
options.D: By waiting for international agencies to take over

explanation: Accurate daily documentation by nurses creates a reliable foundation for institutional data use. [learn more](GST319_U1_T1#GST319_U1_T1_h5)
